page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache. The instance includes hardware cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI alongside standard AVX instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 support. Hardware accelerators are absent with zero GPUs, and no local instance storage is bundled, requiring reliance on external block storage. Network performance is provisioned with a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results reflect the configuration trade-offs inherent in this generation of hardware. Single-core performance shows moderate output, logging 1237.0 on Geekbench and an average-tier score of 4228.49 on PassMark CPU encryption tests. However, multi-threaded throughput falls behind newer architectures, with multi-core Geekbench registering 2816.0 and stress-ng multi-core testing placing in the lower percentiles. Memory subsystem benchmarks show an average PassMark memory score of 2075.12, with uncached read throughput measuring 29.06 GB/sec and write throughput reaching 15.26 GB/sec. Data manipulation workloads display mixed results: single-threaded gzip compression performs adequately at 23.87 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 3.85 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r6a.xlarge provides an economical path to high memory capacity per core without the cost overhead of specialized acceleration hardware or premium compute tiers. The primary trade-off centers on raw compute throughput versus memory volume; compute-heavy tasks encounter bottlenecks due to modest CPU performance and the absence of high-density vector extensions. As a result, this instance is suited for memory-bound applications with moderate processing demands, such as in-memory caches, staging environments, distributed data processing nodes, and medium-scale backend databases relying on network-attached storage.
